summary: If someone sells seeds or grain and the buyer plants them and they do not grow, the seller does not have to pay, since the buyer might have bought them to eat. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says that garden seeds, which are not eaten, must grow, or the seller pays.

chunks.en: Someone who sells produce to his friend and it did not sprout,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells produce to another that is sometimes purchased for consumption and sometimes for planting, and the buyer planted it and it did not sprout,

chunks.en: even flax seeds,
chunks.st: and even if he had sold flaxseeds, which are only occasionally eaten,

chunks.en: does not have to pay for them.
chunks.explain: The buyer did not say he wanted them for planting.
chunks.st: the seller does not bear financial responsibility for them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he is not required to compensate the buyer. Since the buyer did not specify that he purchased the produce in order to plant it, the seller can claim that he assumed the buyer intended to eat it.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Garden seeds, which are not eaten,
chunks.st: If he had sold seeds for garden plants, which are not eaten at all,

chunks.en: he does have to pay for them.
chunks.st: then the seller bears financial responsibility for them,
chunks.stMore: as they were certainly purchased for planting.

summary: When someone buys a large amount of food, he must accept that a small part may be dirty or spoiled. The mishnah lists how much is normal for grain, figs, and barrels of wine.
stIntro: When selling a significant quantity of produce or a number of items, there is a possibility that there will be a certain proportion of impurities in it or that some of the product will be of substandard quality. The mishna delineates what proportion is considered acceptable, for which a buyer may not demand compensation. With regard to

chunks.en: Someone who sells produce to his friend:
chunks.st: one who sells produce, i.e., grain, to another,

chunks.en: the buyer accepts
chunks.st: this buyer accepts upon himself

chunks.en: a quarter kav of dirt in each se'ah.
chunks.st: that up to a quarter-kav of impurities may be present in each se’a of produce purchased.

words.note: A se'ah is a measure of grain, six kav.

chunks.he: תְּאֵנִים, מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֶשֶׂר מְתֻלָּעוֹת לְמֵאָה.
chunks.en: With figs, he accepts ten wormy ones in a hundred.
chunks.st: When purchasing figs, he accepts upon himself that up to ten infested figs may be present in each hundred figs purchased.

chunks.en: With a cellar of wine,
chunks.st: When purchasing a cellar containing barrels of wine,

chunks.en: he accepts ten sour barrels in a hundred.
chunks.st: he accepts upon himself that up to ten barrels of souring wine may be present in each hundred barrels purchased.

chunks.en: With jugs of wine in the Sharon,
chunks.st: When purchasing jugs of wine in the Sharon region,

chunks.en: he accepts ten poor ones in a hundred.
chunks.st: he accepts upon himself that up to ten inferior-quality jugs [pitasot] of wine may be present in each hundred jugs purchased.

summary: If someone sells wine and it turns sour, the seller does not pay, unless his wine is known to go sour. If he said it was spiced or old wine, it must be what he promised.

chunks.en: Someone who sells wine to his friend, and it turned sour,
chunks.st: If one sells wine to another and then it sours,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay for it.
chunks.st: the seller does not bear financial responsibility for its loss.

chunks.en: But if everyone knows that his wine turns sour,
chunks.st: But if it is known of this seller that his wine always sours,

chunks.en: this is a mistaken sale.
chunks.explain: So the sale can be undone.
chunks.st: then this sale is a mistaken transaction,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one based upon false assumptions, as the buyer intended to purchase wine that would maintain its quality; therefore, the seller must reimburse the buyer.

chunks.en: And if he said to him,
chunks.st: And if the seller said to the buyer:

chunks.en: I am selling you spiced wine,
chunks.st: It is wine that is spiced, which is preserved and of lasting quality, that I am selling to you,

chunks.en: he must make sure it lasts until Shavuos.
chunks.st: then he bears financial responsibility to provide him with wine that will keep until the festival of Shavuot.

chunks.en: Old wine means from last year.
chunks.st: And if the seller said: I am selling you old wine, he is responsible to provide wine from the previous year.

chunks.en: And very old wine means from three years before.
chunks.st: And if he said: I am selling you aged wine, he is responsible to provide wine that is from three years earlier.

summary: If someone sells land to build a house for a son's wedding or for a widowed daughter, Rabbi Akiva says it must be four by six amos. Rabbi Yishmael says that is only a cow barn, and the mishnah lists sizes of houses, saying a room's height is half its length plus half its width, like the Heichal.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר מָקוֹם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לִבְנוֹת לוֹ בַיִת,
chunks.en: Someone who sells a place to his friend to build a house,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells a plot of land to another,
chunks.stMore: with the buyer intending to build a bridal house for his son or a widowhood home for his daughter on that plot,

chunks.en: and also one who agrees to build for his friend
chunks.st: and similarly, with regard to a contractor who receives a plot of land from another under a commission to build for the owner on that land

chunks.en: a wedding house for his son
chunks.st: a bridal house for his son,

chunks.en: or a house for his widowed daughter,
chunks.st: or a widowhood home for his daughter,
chunks.stMore: the terms of the transaction are a matter of dispute. The mishna presents the dispute: In the latter case, the contractor must

chunks.en: builds four amos by six,
chunks.st: build a building that is at least four cubits by six
chunks.stMore: cubits in size, and similarly, in the case of the sale, the seller must provide a plot of land that can accommodate a building of that size;

chunks.en: the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: That is a cow barn!
chunks.st: A structure of this size is a cowshed,
chunks.stMore: and a bridal house or a widowhood home is larger than that.

chunks.en: Someone who wants to make a cow barn
chunks.st: One who wants to construct a cowshed

chunks.en: builds four amos by six.
chunks.st: builds a structure at least four cubits by six
chunks.stMore: cubits in size. The mishna delineates the standard dimensions for various other structures.

chunks.en: A small house
chunks.st: A small house is

chunks.en: is six by eight.
chunks.st: six by eight cubits.

chunks.en: A big one, eight by ten.
chunks.st: A large house is eight by ten cubits.

chunks.en: A big hall, ten by ten.
chunks.st: A banquet hall [teraklin] is ten by ten cubits.

chunks.en: Its height is half its length plus half its width.
chunks.st: The standard height for each of these structures is equal to the sum of half its length and half its width.

chunks.en: A proof for this is the Heichal.
chunks.st: There is a proof of the matter;

words.note: The main building of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Everything follows the building of the Heichal.
chunks.st: The proportions are like the building of the Sanctuary;
chunks.stMore: it was forty cubits wide and twenty cubits long and its height was thirty cubits, which is the sum of half the width and half the length.

summary: Someone who owns a well inside his neighbor's house may go in and out only at normal times, and may not bring his animal inside to drink. Each of them may put a lock on it.

chunks.en: Someone who has a well
chunks.st: One who has ownership of a cistern located

chunks.en: inside his neighbor's house
chunks.st: beyond the house of another,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the cistern can be accessed only by entering the property of the other, and also has access rights to that cistern,

chunks.he: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִין
chunks.en: goes in at a time when people usually go in
chunks.st: may enter the house to access his cistern only at a time when it is usual for people to enter,

chunks.he: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין,
chunks.en: and goes out at a time when people usually go out.
chunks.st: and may leave only at a time when it is usual for people to leave.

chunks.en: And he does not bring his animal in to drink from his well,
chunks.st: And in addition, he may not bring his animal into the house and water it from his cistern;

chunks.en: but he fills a pail and gives it water outside.
chunks.st: rather, he must fill a pail with water from the cistern and water his animal outside.

chunks.en: And this one makes himself a lock,
chunks.st: And this one, the owner of the cistern, constructs for himself a lock
chunks.stMore: on the entrance to the cistern to prevent the homeowner from drawing water from it,

chunks.en: and that one makes himself a lock.
chunks.st: and that one, the homeowner, constructs for himself a lock.

summary: Someone who owns a garden inside his neighbor's garden may walk through only at normal times, may not bring buyers in, and may not use it as a shortcut. If they both agreed on a side path, he may come and go as he likes and bring buyers in.

chunks.en: Someone who has a garden
chunks.st: One who has ownership of a garden located

chunks.en: inside his neighbor's garden
chunks.st: beyond the garden of another, and also has access rights to it,

chunks.he: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִים
chunks.en: goes in at a time when people usually go in
chunks.st: may enter his garden only at a time when it is usual for people to enter,

chunks.he: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין,
chunks.en: and goes out at a time when people usually go out.
chunks.st: and may leave only at a time when it is usual for people to leave.

chunks.en: He may not bring merchants into it,
chunks.st: Furthermore, he may not bring merchants into his garden,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִכָּנֵס מִתּוֹכָהּ לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת,
chunks.en: and he may not go through it into another field.
chunks.st: and he may not enter the garden solely in order to use it as a passageway, to enter from it into another field.

chunks.en: And the outer one may plant on the path.
chunks.st: And the owner of the outer garden may sow the path leading to the inner garden.

chunks.en: If they gave him a path from the side
chunks.st: If the court gave him an access path from the side of the outer garden,

chunks.en: with both of them agreeing,
chunks.st: with the agreement of both of them,

chunks.en: he goes in whenever he wants,
chunks.st: he may enter at any time he wants,

chunks.en: and goes out whenever he wants,
chunks.st: and leave at any time he wants,

chunks.en: and he may bring merchants into it.
chunks.st: and may bring merchants into the inner garden.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִכָּנֵס מִתּוֹכָהּ לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת,
chunks.en: But he may not go through it into another field.
chunks.st: But he may still not enter the garden solely in order to enter from it into another field.

chunks.en: And neither of them may plant it.
chunks.st: In such a case, neither this one, the owner of the inner garden, nor that one, the owner of the outer garden, is permitted to plant that side path.

summary: If a public path ran through someone's field and he moved it to the side, he may not take back the old path. The mishnah gives the sizes of a private path, a public road, and other paths.

chunks.en: Someone who had a public road
chunks.st: In the case of one who had a public thoroughfare

chunks.en: going through his field,
chunks.st: passing through his field,

chunks.en: and he took it and gave them a path on the side:
chunks.st: and he appropriated it and instead gave the public an alternative thoroughfare on the side of his property,

chunks.en: what he gave, he gave,
chunks.st: the halakha is that the thoroughfare that he gave them, he gave them, and they may use it.

chunks.en: and his own does not come back to him.
chunks.explain: Now the people may use both paths.
chunks.st: But the original thoroughfare that he took for himself has not reached him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he cannot appropriate it for his personal use.

chunks.en: A private path
chunks.st: The standard width of a private path

chunks.en: is four amos wide.
chunks.st: is four cubits.
chunks.stMore: If a field owner sells the right to pass through his field to an individual, without specifying the width of the path, he must provide him with a path four cubits wide.

chunks.en: A public road
chunks.st: The standard width of a public thoroughfare

chunks.en: is sixteen amos.
chunks.st: is sixteen cubits.

chunks.en: The king's road
chunks.st: The width of a king’s thoroughfare

chunks.en: has no size limit.
chunks.st: has no maximum measure,
chunks.stMore: as the king may appropriate whatever width thoroughfare he wishes.

chunks.en: The path to a grave
chunks.st: The width of the path for the burial procession to a grave

chunks.en: has no size limit.
chunks.st: has no maximum measure.

chunks.en: The place where people stand to comfort mourners: the judges of Tzippori said,
chunks.st: With regard to the practice of standing and comforting the mourners following a funeral, the judges of Tzippori said

chunks.en: a place for planting four kav.
chunks.st: that the standard requisite size is the area required for sowing four kav of seed.

summary: Someone who sells land for a family burial cave must make it a certain size, with a set number of places inside. The Rabbis argue about the sizes, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it all depends on how strong the rock is.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר מָקוֹם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ קֶבֶר,
chunks.en: Someone who sells a place to his friend to make a burial cave,
chunks.st: There is the case of one who sells a plot of land to another in order for him to construct for himself an underground catacomb,

chunks.he: וְכֵן הַמְקַבֵּל מֵחֲבֵרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ קֶבֶר,
chunks.en: and also one who agrees to make a burial cave for his friend,
chunks.st: and similarly the case of a contractor who receives a plot of land from another under a commission to construct for him a catacomb.

chunks.en: makes the inside of the cave
chunks.st: If the size of the catacomb was not specified, then he should make the inside of each burial chamber

chunks.en: four amos by six,
chunks.st: four cubits wide by six cubits long

chunks.en: and opens up eight spaces into it,
chunks.st: and open up into the chamber, by digging into its walls, eight burial niches [kukhin] in which the coffins will rest.

words.note: Long holes dug in the wall of the cave.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִכָּאן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִכָּאן וּשְׁנַיִם מִכְּנֶגְדָּן,
chunks.en: three on this side, three on that side, and two across from them.
chunks.st: Three niches should be opened up from the wall here, along the length of the chamber, and three from there, along the other side, and two niches from the wall facing the entrance.

chunks.en: The spaces are four amos long,
chunks.st: And these niches should be formed so that their length is four cubits

chunks.en: seven tefachim high and six wide.
chunks.st: and their height is seven handbreadths, and their width is six handbreadths.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: He makes the inside of the cave
chunks.st: He should construct the inside of each burial chamber

chunks.en: six amos by eight,
chunks.st: six cubits wide by eight cubits long

chunks.en: and opens up thirteen spaces into it,
chunks.st: and open up into the chamber, by digging into its walls, thirteen burial niches.

chunks.he: אַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן וְאַרְבָּעָה מִכָּאן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה מִכְּנֶגְדָּן
chunks.en: four on this side, four on that side, three across from them,
chunks.st: Four niches should be opened up from the wall here, along the length of the chamber, and four from there, along the other side, and three niches from the wall facing the entrance,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מִימִין הַפֶּתַח וְאֶחָד מִן הַשְּׂמֹאל.
chunks.en: one on the right of the door and one on the left.
chunks.st: and one from the right of the entrance and another one from the left.
chunks.stMore: The mishna describes the general structure of the catacomb:

chunks.en: And he makes a yard at the opening of the cave
chunks.st: And he must fashion a courtyard at the entrance of the burial chamber

chunks.en: six by six,
chunks.st: that should be six cubits by six cubits,

chunks.en: as big as the bed and the people carrying it.
chunks.st: which is equal to the combined length of the bier of the deceased and those who bury him,
chunks.stMore: to ensure adequate room for the burial to take place.

chunks.en: And he opens up two caves into it,
chunks.st: And he should open up two burial chambers into the courtyard,

chunks.en: one on this side and one on that side.
chunks.st: one from here and one from there, i.e., on opposite sides of the courtyard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Four, one on each of its four sides.
chunks.st: He should open up four burial chambers, one on each of the courtyard’s four sides.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It all depends on the rock.
chunks.st: Everything is dependent on the nature of the bedrock.
chunks.stMore: If the bedrock is hard and strong it will be able to accommodate more niches, which will be more closely packed together, with less bedrock between them. If the bedrock is softer, fewer and more sparsely spaced niches should be formed.
